q: The chemical name of common salt is…
x: NaCl. Do not mix it up with baking soda or washing soda.

q: Bleaching powder is used mainly to…
x: It is calcium oxychloride and gives off chlorine.

q: Plaster of Paris is made by heating…
x: It sets hard with water, so doctors use it for broken bones.

q: Quicklime is…
x: Limestone (calcium carbonate) on heating gives quicklime. With water it becomes slaked lime.

q: Caustic soda is…
x: It is used to make soap and paper.

q: The gas known as laughing gas is…
x: N₂O. Dentists once used it to dull pain.

q: Dry ice is solid…
x: It turns straight into gas without melting, so it keeps things cold and dry.

q: Which gas is filled in electric bulbs?
x: Argon (often with nitrogen) does not react with the hot wire.

q: The wire inside an ordinary electric bulb is made of…
x: Tungsten has a very high melting point.

q: The heating coil of an electric heater is made of…
x: Nichrome has high resistance and does not rust when hot.

q: A fuse wire should have…
x: It melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows.

q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
x: Mercury. Bromine is the liquid non-metal.

q: Which is the lightest gas?
x: Hydrogen is lightest, but balloons use helium because it does not burn.

q: The hardest natural substance is…
x: Diamond and graphite are both forms of carbon.

q: Pencil "lead" is made of…
x: Graphite mixed with clay. It has no lead in it.

q: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
x: Silver is best, but copper is used in wires because it is cheaper.

q: Rusting of iron needs…
x: Rust is iron oxide. Paint or zinc coating keeps air and water away.

q: Coating iron with zinc to stop rust is called…
x: Vulcanisation is hardening rubber with sulphur.

q: Brass is an alloy of…
x: Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze = copper + tin.

q: Bronze is an alloy of…
x: Bronze was the first alloy made by humans.

q: Stainless steel does not rust because it contains…
x: Steel is iron with carbon; chromium and nickel make it stainless.

q: The acid in lemon and orange is…
x: Citric in citrus fruits. Tartaric in tamarind and grapes.

q: The acid in sour milk and curd is…
x: Lactic acid is made by bacteria in milk.

q: The sting of an ant contains…
x: "Formica" is Latin for ant.

q: The acid in our stomach that helps digestion is…
x: Antacid tablets are mild bases that cancel extra acid.

q: The pH of pure water is…
x: Below 7 is acid; above 7 is base.

q: Blue litmus paper turns red in…
x: Acid turns blue to red. Base turns red to blue.

q: Which gas do plants take in to make food?
x: In photosynthesis, plants use carbon dioxide, water and sunlight and give out oxygen.

q: The green colour of leaves comes from…
x: Chlorophyll traps sunlight for photosynthesis.

q: Which part of the cell is called its "powerhouse"?
x: Mitochondria release energy from food.

q: The red colour of blood comes from…
x: Haemoglobin contains iron and carries oxygen.

q: Which blood cells fight germs?
x: Red cells carry oxygen; platelets help clotting; white cells fight infection.

q: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
x: O negative can be given to anyone. AB positive can receive from anyone.

q: Which blood group is the universal receiver?
x: AB has no antibodies against A or B blood.

q: The largest gland in the human body is the…
x: The liver makes bile. The skin is the largest organ.

q: Insulin is made in the…
x: Too little insulin causes diabetes.

q: Lack of iodine causes…
x: The thyroid gland in the neck swells. That is why salt is iodised.

q: Lack of iron causes…
x: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin.

q: How many bones does an adult human have?
x: A baby is born with about 300; many join together later.

q: The longest bone in the human body is the…
x: The smallest bone is the stapes, in the ear.

q: The normal human body temperature is about…
How many chambers does the human heart have?
x: Two upper chambers (atria) and two lower ones (ventricles).

q: Blood pressure is measured with a…
x: A stethoscope is for listening to the heart and lungs.

q: Which organ filters waste from the blood and makes urine?
x: Dialysis is done when the kidneys fail.

q: Which vitamin is made in the skin in sunlight?
x: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium for bones.

q: Lack of vitamin B12 causes…
x: B12 is found mostly in animal foods such as milk, eggs and meat.

q: AIDS is caused by…
x: HIV attacks the body's defence system. World AIDS Day is 1 December.

q: Tuberculosis mainly affects the…
x: It is caused by a bacterium and spreads through the air. The BCG vaccine protects against it.

q: The BCG vaccine is given against…
x: It is given to babies soon after birth.

q: Rabies spreads through…
o: The bite of an infected dog or other animal
x: It is a viral disease. Louis Pasteur made the first rabies vaccine.

q: Which disease is caused by a fungus?
x: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection, not a worm.

q: Jaundice mainly affects the…
x: The skin and eyes turn yellow. Hepatitis is one cause.

q: Who gave the theory of evolution by natural selection?
x: In "On the Origin of Species" (1859).

q: Who is called the father of genetics?
x: He worked on pea plants. Watson and Crick found the shape of DNA.

q: Heating milk to kill germs without boiling it away is called…
x: Named after Louis Pasteur.

q: Curd is formed from milk by…
x: The bacteria turn milk sugar into lactic acid.

q: Bread rises because yeast gives off…
x: Yeast is a fungus. This process is fermentation.

q: The SI unit of force is the…
x: Joule = energy. Watt = power. Pascal = pressure.

q: The SI unit of electric current is the…
x: Volt = potential difference. Ohm = resistance.

q: The unit used on a home electricity bill is the…
x: One "unit" is one kilowatt-hour of energy.

q: Loudness of sound is measured in…
x: Hertz measures frequency (pitch).

q: Sound cannot travel through…
x: Sound needs a medium. It is fastest in solids.

q: Sound travels fastest in…
x: Solids, then liquids, then gases.

q: The speed of light is about…
x: 330 m/s is roughly the speed of sound in air.

q: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
x: A convex mirror shows a wider area, though things look smaller.

q: A dentist's small mirror and a shaving mirror are…
x: A concave mirror gives a bigger image when the object is close.

q: Short-sightedness (myopia) is corrected with a…
x: Myopia: far things look blurred. Long-sightedness needs a convex lens.

q: A stick half-dipped in water looks bent because of…
x: Light changes direction when it passes from water to air.

q: Optical fibres, used for fast internet, work on…
x: Light bounces inside the thin glass fibre without leaking out.

q: The sun looks red at sunrise and sunset because red light…
x: Blue is scattered away on the long path through the air; red reaches the eye.

q: Cooking is faster in a pressure cooker because high pressure…
o: Raises the boiling point of water
Lowers the boiling point of water
x: Water boils above 100 °C inside the cooker.

q: On a high mountain, food takes longer to cook because…
o: There is less oxygen in food
x: Air pressure is low, so the boiling point falls.

q: Ice floats on water because…
o: Ice is less dense than water
x: Water is densest at 4 °C.

q: White clothes are better in summer because they…
x: Dark colours absorb heat; light colours reflect it.

q: Water in an earthen pot stays cool because of…
x: Water seeps out through tiny holes and evaporates, taking heat away.

q: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by…
x: Radiation needs no medium, so it can cross empty space.

q: A thermos flask keeps tea hot by cutting down…
x: The vacuum stops conduction and convection; the silver coating stops radiation.

q: A device that changes mechanical energy into electrical energy is a…
x: A motor does the opposite: electricity to motion.

q: A transformer is used to…
x: A rectifier changes AC to DC.

q: In a solar cell, sunlight is turned into…
x: Solar cells are made mostly of silicon.

q: Which fuel is used in most nuclear power plants?
x: India has large thorium sands in Kerala and Odisha for the future.

q: A nuclear reactor and the atom bomb work on…
x: Fission = splitting a heavy atom. Fusion = joining light atoms, as in the Sun and the hydrogen bomb.

q: The Sun gets its energy from…
x: Hydrogen nuclei join to make helium.

q: India's first nuclear test (1974) was done at…
x: In Rajasthan, code name "Smiling Buddha". The second round was in 1998.

q: Who is called the father of India's nuclear programme?
x: The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in Mumbai is named after him.

q: C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in…
x: For the Raman Effect (scattering of light). Tagore won in 1913 for literature.

q: Who discovered the electron?
x: Thomson: electron. Rutherford: nucleus and proton. Chadwick: neutron.

q: Who gave the laws of motion and gravitation?
x: Einstein gave the theory of relativity.

q: Who invented the radio?
x: J.C. Bose of India also did early work on radio waves. Baird invented television.

q: Who invented dynamite?
x: The Nobel Prizes were started with his money.

q: Who discovered radioactivity?
x: Becquerel in 1896. Marie Curie found radium and polonium.

q: The "brain" of a computer is the…
x: Central Processing Unit.

q: 1 kilobyte is equal to…
x: 8 bits = 1 byte. 1,024 KB = 1 MB.

q: Which memory is wiped when the computer is switched off?
x: RAM is temporary (volatile) memory.

q: "HTTP" in a web address stands for…
x: HTTPS is the secure form.

q: India's first supercomputer was…
x: Built by C-DAC, Pune, in 1991.

q: Which gas is used to ripen fruits?
x: Ethylene is a natural plant hormone.

q: The gas that leaked in the Bhopal tragedy of 1984 was…
x: From the Union Carbide pesticide plant, on the night of 2–3 December 1984.

q: Which gas from car exhaust stops blood from carrying oxygen?
x: It has no colour or smell, which makes it very dangerous.

q: Biogas (gobar gas) is mostly…
x: Made when cow dung rots without air.

q: Which metal poisoning caused Minamata disease in Japan?
x: Cadmium causes Itai-itai disease.

q: Arsenic in ground water is a serious problem mainly in…
x: Too much fluoride in water, on the other hand, harms teeth and bones (fluorosis).

q: Too much fluoride in drinking water causes…
x: Parts of Odisha, such as Nuapada, face this problem.
